title: Machine slide hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Repaired port-level topology for a fixed-pump two-speed machine-slide circuit. The circuit uses an open tank, fixed-displacement pump, main relief, tandem-centre 4/3 DCV, double-acting slide cylinder, one rod-side one-way flow control, a pressure-opened sequence valve in the working-feed rod-exhaust path, and a mechanically position-operated rapid bypass in parallel with that sequenced metered path. During rapid approach the DCV extends the cylinder, the RapidBypassValve is open, and the ContactSequenceValve remains closed so rod exhaust has an unrestricted bypass path. During working feed the bypass is mechanically closed and the pressure-opened sequence valve enables rod exhaust through the single metering element. During return the DCV retracts the cylinder and reverse-flow paths through the one-way flow control and sequence valve preserve powered retraction without adding a separate return control.

selected_components.name: Double-Acting Cylinder

bore, rod and stroke deferred to sizing

motion_control_decisions.justification: This is the faster phase in the same advance direction before the specified load/contact-induced slow feed; load is stated as resistive and no holding or overrunning condition is specified.

The speed reduction is explicitly required to result from the increased load/contact condition without an electrical pressure switch. For a horizontal resistive slide with deliberate throttling, meter-out control of rod-side exhaust during extension is the conventional inferred default.
Only return travel and resisting load are specified; no return speed control, holding, or overrunning condition is stated.

component_states.reason: Extend state connects P-A and B-T for cylinder extension.

phase_configurations.notes: Rapid approach uses DCV extend with the position-operated bypass open. Rod-side exhaust can flow SlideCylinder.Rod -> RapidBypassValve.P -> RapidBypassValve.A -> DCV.B -> DCV.T -> Tank.R while the pressure-opened sequence feed path remains closed.

component_states.reason: Extend state keeps cap chamber supplied and rod branch exhausting to tank through B-T.
At/after the contact trip the rapid bypass is closed so it cannot defeat the required working-feed meter-out control.
Load/contact pressure at X opens P-A, enabling the sequenced rod-exhaust path through FeedFlowControl.

phase_configurations.notes: Working feed closes the unmetered bypass and opens the pressure-sequenced feed path. The intended rod exhaust path is SlideCylinder.Rod -> ContactSequenceValve.P -> ContactSequenceValve.A -> FeedFlowControl.A -> FeedFlowControl.B -> DCV.B -> DCV.T -> Tank.R.

component_states.reason: Retract state connects P-B and A-T for powered retraction.
No rapid-bypass function is required for return; leaving the mechanically tripped bypass closed does not prevent the free reverse return path through the selected feed branch.
With cap-side pressure vented during retraction, the sequence valve may be in its closed/default state while preserving its A-to-P reverse check path.

phase_configurations.notes: Return is sizing_only with no dedicated return speed control. Pressure from DCV.B reaches the rod chamber through FeedFlowControl free reverse B-to-A and ContactSequenceValve reverse check A-to-P; cap exhaust flows SlideCylinder.Cap -> DCV.A -> DCV.T -> Tank.R.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power unit with tank suction and direct pump pressure branch
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S; Pump.P provides the pressure source for the relief valve and the DCV branch in an open-circuit hydraulic supply.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Main relief from pump pressure to tank return
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Pump.P is connected directly to ReliefValve.P and ReliefValve.T returns to Tank.R; the relief setting is deferred to sizing/commissioning but specified not to exceed 20 bar.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Double-acting cylinder controlled by 4/3 tandem-centre DCV
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DCV extend supplies the cap chamber and exhausts the rod branch for advance/feed; DCV retract supplies the rod branch and exhausts the cap chamber for full return; neutral unloads the fixed pump through P-T while blocking A and B.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Pressure-opened feed-enable valve in the rod-side working-feed exhaust path
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ContactSequenceValve.P is connected to the rod-side exhaust node, A feeds FeedFlowControl.A, X senses cap/advance pressure, and T drains to tank. It is closed before contact/load pressure and opens after the pressure trigger to enable the working-feed path hydraulically.

FeedFlowControl is placed downstream of ContactSequenceValve in the rod-side exhaust path with A toward the cylinder/sequence side and B toward DCV.B, so extension rod exhaust is metered A-to-B during working feed while reverse retraction supply is free B-to-A.

RapidBypassValve.P is connected to the rod-side exhaust node and A rejoins DCV.B. It is open before contact/trip for unrestricted rapid approach and closed during working feed so no unmetered bypass remains around FeedFlowControl.

design_decisions.decision: Use an open-circuit tank, fixed-displacement pump, and main relief valve.
design_decisions.rationale: The brief requires an open-circuit power unit and pressure limitation not above 20 bar. The selected fixed pump is appropriate because no standby-efficiency requirement was stated, and the tandem-centre DCV unloads the fixed pump in neutral.

design_decisions.decision: Use a 4/3 tandem-centre DCV for slide direction control and fixed-pump unloading in neutral.
design_decisions.rationale: The DCV provides powered extension and powered retraction of the double-acting slide cylinder. Tandem centre unloads Pump.P to Tank.R in neutral while blocking work ports, which is suitable for a horizontal resistive slide with no separate load-holding requirement.

design_decisions.decision: Place exactly one one-way flow control in the rod-side exhaust path for working feed.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed working-feed decision requires non-compensated load-sensitive meter-out control of the rod chamber during extension. Orienting A toward the sequence/cylinder side and B toward DCV.B makes A-to-B the metered extension exhaust direction and B-to-A the free reverse direction for retraction.

design_decisions.decision: Use the externally piloted sequence valve as a pressure-opened working-feed enable valve, not as a pressure-closing rapid bypass.
design_decisions.rationale: The supplied catalog state behavior for the selected sequence valve is closed before trigger and open after trigger. Moving it into the working-feed rod-exhaust path aligns the topology with that behavior: rapid approach is not forced through this closed branch, and after contact/load pressure rises the metered feed path is enabled.

design_decisions.decision: Add a position-operated bypass for rapid approach and close it for working feed.
design_decisions.rationale: Because the selected sequence valve is pressure-opening, a separate selected position-operated bypass supplies the required open-before/closed-after rapid path. Closing this bypass during working feed ensures the typed meter-out path cannot be defeated by an unmetered parallel rod-exhaust route.

assumptions: Slide advance and working feed are cylinder extension; full return is cylinder retraction.
The slide load is horizontal/resistive, so no counterbalance or load-lock valve is required.
Relief pressure, pump flow, cylinder dimensions, feed-control setting, sequence setting, and rapid-bypass trip point are sizing/commissioning tasks.
The RapidBypassValve trip is commissioned so the bypass is closed at the start of slide_working_feed.
open_issues: The RapidBypassValve trip must be arranged so the bypass is closed at the start of slide_working_feed; this is a commissioning/mechanical-interface condition, not a separate hydraulic component.

Sizing must verify cylinder areas, pump flow, relief setting, flow-control setting and sequence setting for 2.5 kN rapid approach, 12.5 kN working feed, 25 mm/s approach, 8.33 mm/s feed and maximum 20 bar pressure.
Return initiation is not specified; this topology provides commanded powered retraction but not automatic return sequencing.
Meter-out working feed can create rod-side back pressure and pressure intensification; selected cylinder area ratio, loads and valve ratings must be checked before build.

The rapid-to-working-feed transition is not reliably caused by the hydraulic load/contact condition through the sequence valve. ContactSequenceValve only opens the metered branch; it does not close the unmetered rapid path. The actual removal of the rapid bypass depends on RapidBypassValve being mechanically/position operated. If load/contact pressure occurs before that trip, the unmetered bypass remains open and working feed is bypassed; if the position trip occurs without true workpiece load, the blocked exhaust can raise pressure and open the sequence valve anyway. This violates the brief requirement for a load/contact-induced hydraulic sequence transition without a separate position-based phase change.

RapidBypassValve is an added rapid-approach control/bypass around the declared rod-side meter-out path. The brief explicitly directs not to add separate approach/return controls unless another typed phase requires them, and requires the sequence valve to provide the load/contact-induced transition. This topology instead uses an additional position-operated bypass as an independent phase-change element, adding unjustified functional complexity and defeating the intended sequence-valve-only transition logic.

research_coverage.summary: The accumulated evidence supports several core principles—relief valve protection to tank, return flow to reservoir, double-acting cylinder with 4-way directional control, meter-out working-feed throttling at the rod-side exhaust during extension, reverse-flow check bypass for return, and pressure sequence valves as hydraulic-only load/pressure-triggered devices. However, the evidence is not yet sufficient to design the requested topology safely and unambiguously because critical connection logic is still missing for the pump suction path, neutral directional-valve behavior/port mapping, and especially the automatic rapid-approach-to-slow-feed transition: the findings show that a sequence valve can open a secondary branch when pressure rises, but do not prove how the unrestricted rapid path is closed or otherwise prevented from bypassing the meter-out feed restriction after load contact.

items.rationale: Covered for pump outlet/high-pressure side, return line to reservoir, relief valve opening at preset pressure and diverting to reservoir, fixed-displacement pump relief requirement, and external relief drain-to-tank/return guidance. Not fully covered because this need explicitly requires a complete suction, pump, relief, return, and reservoir topology, and the findings themselves state that the tank/reservoir-to-pump suction line is not directly documented by a cited source.

Covered for using a double-acting cylinder, a four-way/4/3 directional-control valve, and spring centering to neutral. Not fully covered because the findings do not establish the essential P/T/A/B connection logic for extension versus retraction, nor do they support a specific neutral-center spool arrangement for safe neutral behavior in this fixed-displacement open circuit. The current evidence explicitly says it is insufficient to choose among open, closed, tandem, or float center configurations.

Covered for the working-feed subpattern: meter-out speed control, throttling the rod-end exhaust during extension, avoiding an unmetered bypass during feed, and using a reverse-flow check for free return. Also partly covered for pressure-triggered phase change by sequence valve. Not fully covered because the rapid-approach and automatic transition topology remains ambiguous: the evidence does not show how the unrestricted rapid approach path is disabled or made subordinate once load/contact pressure rises, so the slow meter-out feed would not necessarily control speed after the sequence valve opens. Full-return behavior is partly inferable from double-acting cylinder/DCV and check-bypass evidence, but the complete ordered rapid/feed/return circuit is not yet supported.

Covered for the general principle that a pressure sequence valve can provide hydraulic-only sequencing without an electrical pressure switch and can respond to load/resistance-caused pressure rise. Not fully covered because the accumulated findings only support opening or enabling a secondary branch; they do not cite a two-speed force/load-switching circuit that changes from unrestricted fast approach to throttled slow feed by closing, unloading, blocking, or otherwise neutralizing the rapid path. Without that missing connection principle, the topology could leave the rapid path open and bypass the slow-feed restriction, which is safety- and function-critical.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing cited claim for reservoir/tank outlet feeding the pump inlet through a suction line in an open hydraulic circuit.

Missing cited directional-valve port map for extending and retracting a double-acting cylinder, and missing supported selection of a safe neutral-center configuration for this open circuit with fixed-displacement pump and relief protection.

Missing cited two-speed hydraulic circuit logic showing how rapid extension is unrestricted during approach but is automatically replaced by a throttled working feed when load/contact pressure rises, without an electrical pressure switch.
Missing cited connection principle showing that the rapid-flow/bypass path is closed, unloaded, or otherwise prevented from bypassing the meter-out restriction during the working-feed phase.

The research synthesis does not cite one complete manufacturer/application schematic for the composed two-speed slide circuit. This is nonblocking for a valid generic topology, but targeted evidence would be useful after correcting the transition method.

design_review.summary: Invalid. The open-circuit supply, relief, directional extend/retract paths, rod-side meter-out element, sequence-valve drain, and declared return path are broadly covered, but the proposed pressure-opened sequence valve plus mechanically position-operated rapid bypass does not satisfy the required hydraulic load/contact-induced rapid-to-working-feed transition and introduces a prohibited separate approach control.

The open-circuit supply, relief, directional extend/retract paths, rod-side meter-out element, sequence-valve drain, and declared return path are broadly covered, but the proposed pressure-opened sequence valve plus mechanically position-operated rapid bypass does not satisfy the required hydraulic load/contact-induced rapid-to-working-feed transition and introduces a prohibited separate approach control.
